# Editors and drive apps

An editor is a `powerhouse/document-editor` document in the Vetra drive; a drive app is a `powerhouse/app` document. Codegen writes the code once the document is CONFIRMED. Never write the scaffold by hand; for an app, don't use `ph generate app` either. Your work is the UI inside the generated files.

## Create an editor

1. Check `editors/` for an editor for the document type. If one exists, ask in an interactive session whether to create a new one or reimplement it.
2. `getDocumentModelSchema` with `type: "powerhouse/document-editor"`.
3. `createDocument` with `documentType: "powerhouse/document-editor"` and `driveId` set to the `vetra-<hash>` drive. This adds it to the drive; don't also dispatch `ADD_FILE`.
4. One `addActions` call, scope `global`:
   - `SET_EDITOR_NAME` (`{ name }`)
   - exactly one `ADD_DOCUMENT_TYPE` (`{ id, documentType }`). Codegen does not support an editor for more than one type yet.
   - `SET_EDITOR_STATUS` with `{ status: "CONFIRMED" }`. While DRAFT, or without a document type, codegen writes nothing.
5. Call `getCodegenStatus` with the editor document's `documentId` and `waitSeconds: 60`. Once it is `done`, the editor is in `editors/<editor-id>/` (the id is the kebab-cased name) and registered in `editors/editors.ts`.

## Implement the editor

Codegen writes:

- `editor.tsx`: the editor. Edit this file; don't create a new main component. Keep its default-exported function named `Editor`: codegen keeps a file that has one and rewrites a file that doesn't.
- `module.ts`: rewritten by codegen on every run. Don't edit it.

Put your components in `components/` (create it), one per file. For routes, links to other documents and navigation from an editor, read the customize-connect skill's data-and-navigation guide.

Then:

- Read the schema of the document model the editor is for (`getDocumentModelSchema` with its type, or `document-models/<model>/`).
- Props: `EditorProps<TDocument, TAction>` from `document-model` gives `document` and `dispatch`, typed for the model.
- Render `<DocumentToolbar document={document} />` from `@powerhousedao/design-system/connect` first, at the top, with nothing beside it.
- Child components call `useSelected<Model>Document()`, which returns `[document, dispatch]` for the document the editor was rendered with. Don't pass `document` and `dispatch` down as props.
- Import types, `actions` and hooks from the barrel `document-models/<model>`. There is no `editors/hooks/` folder. `actions` holds the model's actions and the base actions every document has, such as `setName`, which the scaffold's `editor.tsx` uses.
- Ids for new objects come from `generateId()` from `document-model`, passed in the action input.

```tsx
// editors/todo-editor/editor.tsx
import { DocumentToolbar } from "@powerhousedao/design-system/connect";
import type { EditorProps } from "document-model";
import type { TodoAction, TodoDocument } from "document-models/todo";
import { TodoList } from "./components/TodoList.js";

export default function Editor({
  document,
}: EditorProps<TodoDocument, TodoAction>) {
  return (
    <div>
      <DocumentToolbar document={document} />
      <TodoList />
    </div>
  );
}

// editors/todo-editor/components/TodoList.tsx
import { generateId } from "document-model";
import { actions, useSelectedTodoDocument } from "document-models/todo";

export function TodoList() {
  const [document, dispatch] = useSelectedTodoDocument();

  function handleAddTodo(title: string) {
    if (title) dispatch(actions.addTodo({ id: generateId(), title }));
  }
  // ...
}
```

The barrel also exports `use<Model>DocumentById`, `use<Model>DocumentsInSelectedDrive` and `use<Model>DocumentsInSelectedFolder`.

Codegen registers every editor in `editors/editors.ts`; don't edit that file.

## Rejected actions

A reducer that throws, or a write the document's policy refuses, does not apply. To tell the user, pass `dispatch` an `onErrors` callback, as the generated `editor.tsx` does. It gets an `OperationRejectedError` (from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`) per rejected action, or the error that stopped the dispatch:

- `message`: the reducer's error message, or the reason for a denial.
- `actionType`: the action's type.
- `kind`: `"reducer-error"`, or `"denied"` for a write the policy refused.

`onErrors` runs first; `onSuccess` then runs with the document and `{ rejected }`, the actions that were not applied, so clear a form only when `rejected` is empty. The types are in `@powerhousedao/shared/document-model/dispatch`. Clear the message before dispatching:

```tsx
const [error, setError] = useState<string>();

const handleRename = (title: string) => {
  setError(undefined);
  dispatch(actions.setTitle({ title }), (errors) =>
    setError(errors[0]?.message),
  );
};
```

Show the error next to the input that caused it.

## Operation history

In Connect, an editor's `document.operations` holds an empty array per scope, whatever the history. Don't read history or rejected operations from it.

- List operations with `useDocumentOperations(document.header.id, "global")` from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`. Pages arrive oldest first; call `fetchNextPage` while `hasNextPage` is true.
- The operation count of a scope is `document.header.revision.global` (or `[scope]`). It counts that scope's operations, rejected ones included; `revision.document` counts the document's own header operations, such as its creation.
- Connect's revision history view shows a document's operations and their errors.

## Create a drive app

A drive app is the view Connect shows for a drive: an editor module for `powerhouse/document-drive`. Read the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide before you write the app's code: it covers the app's props and the hooks for folders, nodes and navigation.

1. Check `editors/` for an app (its `module.ts` lists `powerhouse/document-drive`). If one exists, ask in an interactive session whether to create a new one or reimplement it.
2. `getDocumentModelSchema` with `type: "powerhouse/app"`.
3. `createDocument` with `documentType: "powerhouse/app"` and `driveId` set to the `vetra-<hash>` drive.
4. One `addActions` call, scope `global`:
   - `SET_APP_NAME` (`{ name }`)
   - `SET_DOCUMENT_TYPES` (`{ documentTypes: [...] }`): the types the app holds. An empty list allows every type.
   - `SET_APP_STATUS` with `{ status: "CONFIRMED" }`. While DRAFT, codegen writes nothing.
5. Codegen writes `editors/<app-id>/`, not `apps/`. The app id is the kebab-cased name. It registers the module in `editors/editors.ts` and `powerhouse.manifest.json`:
   - `editor.tsx`: the app's root.
   - `components/`: a folder tree, folder contents and a create button to start from.
   - `config.ts`: `allowedDocumentTypes` and `isDragAndDropEnabled`.
   - `module.ts`: the module's id, name and document type.

## Implement the drive app

- Codegen writes the scaffold once. While `editor.tsx` has its default-exported `Editor` function, codegen leaves `editor.tsx`, `components/`, `config.ts` and `module.ts` alone and only re-registers the module. Edit them freely.
- Changing the app document's types later does not update `config.ts`. Edit `allowedDocumentTypes` there yourself.
- Read the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide before writing code. It covers the app's props (`document` is the drive, `children` is the open document's editor or `null`), the `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` hooks for folders, nodes and navigation, and how a drive gets its app.

## Attach an app to a drive

A drive shows the app its `header.meta.preferredEditor` names.

- New drive: `addDrive` with `{ "name": "<name>", "preferredEditor": "<app-id>" }`. Vetra Studio lists every drive on the local Switchboard.
- The Vetra Preview drive: set `"vetra": { "previewDrive": { "app": "<app-id>" } }` in `powerhouse.config.json`. `ph vetra` applies it when it starts, so call `restartVetra` after setting it; a fresh clone keeps it.
- Existing drive: `addActions` on the drive with `{ "type": "SET_PREFERRED_EDITOR", "scope": "header", "input": { "preferredEditor": "<app-id>" } }`.

The Create Drive dialog, drives every user gets (`connect.drives.defaultDrives`), setting the app from code and Connect's default view are in the customize-connect skill's drive-apps guide.

Run `npm run tsc` and `npm run lint:fix` after creating or changing an editor or app.
